catalog_citation: Meyer, Julien & Denny Moore. 2021. A flute, musical bows and bamboo clarinets that "speak" in the Amazon rainforest; speech and music in the Gavião language of Rondônia. Frontiers in Psychology 12:674289. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2021.674289 (CC-BY). Supporting: Moore, Denny & Julien Meyer. 2014. The study of tone and related phenomena in an Amazonian tone language: Gavião of Rondônia. Language Documentation & Conservation 8: 613-636. hdl:10125/24618.
catalog_locator: Meyer & Moore 2021, p. 4, col. 1, section 'Some Phonetic and Phonological Characteristics of the Language of the Gavião of Rondônia' (p. 4); supporting Moore & Meyer 2014, pp. 615-616, sec. 3 (p. 4).
catalog_quote: In the phonology there are 18 consonant phonemes, not much different from the consonants of English. There are only five contrastive vowels. Nasalization is contrastive on vowels and spreads to the right under certain conditions. There are no stress contrasts (Moore, 1984). ... The supersegmental phonology is complicated and quite complex to represent in practical transcription. There are contrasts between high, low and rising tones and also between short and long vowels. Long vowels are phonologically different from two short vowels in the same syllable, though they are phonetically the same. Also, some long syllables have a floating low tone finally. A more detailed analysis of the tonal system is given in Moore (1999) and Moore and Meyer (2014). [Meyer & Moore 2021: 4] ... One simple test for checking whether speakers were perceiving tone or perceiving stress involved a minimal pair, ‘fat’ and ‘egg’, given above. When the two syllables were pronounced with low tones but with stress on the second syllable, consultants judged the word to be ‘fat’, giving importance to the tone and not the stress. [Moore & Meyer 2014: 616]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Gavião of Rondônia is a tone-and-length language (short H, L, LH; long constant and long alternating tones with floating L causing downstep); stress is not contrastive. No source opened states a position for any phonetic (non-contrastive) prominence. Supporting first-hand evidence in Moore & Meyer 2014 (LD&C 8: 616): in a perception test consultants classified words by tone and ignored imposed stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the lexical/word phonology (contrasts); co-authored by the primary describer (Moore) and back-referenced to his 1984 dissertation, whose phonology appendix (pp.223-233, scanned) treats only tone/length and does not itself use the word 'stress'.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Gavião (Ikólóéhj / Ikolen, 'Digüt') variety of Terra Indígena Igarapé Lourdes, Rondônia = Glottolog gavi1246 (ISO gvo). Moore 1984 treats Zoró, Cinta Larga and (probably) Aruá as dialects of the same language; Glottolog lists these as separate languoids (zoro1244, cint1239, arua1261) -- the statement quoted is for Gavião proper.

Moscow: Buki Vedi.
tone_statements.quote: Within about three days of linguistic elicitation there had appeared a minimal quadruple of two-syllable words that had the same consonants and vowels. If the difference between the words were stress then there could only be two different words, one with initial stress and one with final stress. Tone differences could be much more complicated. [...] At first it seemed like the tone and length system was just high, low, and rising tones which could be either short or long. But the system was considerably more complex, with the tone changing in certain environments.

tone_statements.citation: Meyer, Julien & Denny Moore. 2013. Arte verbal e música na língua Gavião de Rondônia: metodologia para estudar e documentar a fala tocada com instrumentos musicais. Boletim do Museu Paraense Emílio Goeldi. Ciências Humanas 8(2): 307-324.
tone_statements.quote: Em uma língua com tom e prolongamento distintivos, como Gavião de Rondônia, a primeira questão sobre a fala tocada com instrumentos musicais é a relação entre as melodias e a fonologia suprassegmental das palavras correspondentes na fala cantada e na fala normal.
tone_statements.translation: In a language with distinctive tone and length, such as Gavião of Rondônia, the first question about speech played on musical instruments is the relation between the melodies and the suprasegmental phonology of the corresponding words in sung speech and in normal speech.

sources.note: Secs. 3-4 (pp.615-618): four-way contrast on segmentally identical disyllables shown to be tone, not stress; perception test: 'When the two syllables were pronounced with low tones but with stress on the second syllable, consultants judged the word to be fat, giving importance to the tone and not the stress.' Summarises tone/length system (short L, H, LH; long constant and long alternating tones with floating L, downstep). No statement of where any (non-contrastive) stress falls.
